dedupe_keys.name: wastewaterscan infectious disease wastewater monitoring data

description: WastewaterSCAN is a wastewater monitoring network run by Stanford University and Emory University with Verily that tests settled solids from participating sewage treatment plants for more than a dozen infectious diseases. Its site says samples come from nearly 150 locations in 40 states serving more than 39 million people, and its public dashboard shows national and local levels and trends for influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, human metapneumovirus, norovirus GII, enterovirus D68, mpox, Candidozyma auris, hepatitis A, measles, West Nile virus, rotavirus and parvovirus, expressed as nucleic-acid quantities adjusted by pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV). Research deposits in the Stanford Digital Repository hold concentrations for 191 treatment plants, and WastewaterSCAN rows also flow into CDC's national dataset under CC BY-NC 4.0; research use requires contacting the team. Caveats: results are described as experimental and not for diagnosis, the set of plants changes over time, and dashboard data were not downloaded here. Simulation uses: pathogen signals at treatment-plant level for epidemic early warning and emergency response. Related record: the CDC National Wastewater Surveillance System (data-cdc-nwss-wastewater-surveillance).
